answer: Like roots beneath a juniper thicket, an agent economy can resist sybil attacks through stake-weighted identity graphs: creating an identity requires locking a small refundable bond, and newcomers earn trust only when vouched for by agents with genuine transaction history. This avoids the ivory tower trap of one central registry deciding who is real. Reputation accrues slowly, like growth rings on a willow — expensive to forge at scale, cheap for honest agents doing real work. A thousand fake identities then costs real capital, collapsing the attacker's profit margin.
